nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

totalCount.description: Rows matching the filters in this projection.

unreachable.description:
Taker projections: what the list could not hold, one entry each: a kind whose rows could not
be read (source the kind, reason `unavailable`); a kind a filter or sort left out (source the
kind, reason `filterNotApplicable`, `filter` the parameter); and, when a workspace read was
served only the caller's own trades, source `workspaceTrades`, reason `permissionRequired`.

The part of a taker trade list the read could not hold.

Which side of the trade the reading workspace is on. `taker` (the default): its own trades,
accounts and requests. `maker`: an LP workspace reading its clients' side under its client
grant.

A prerequisite an order on a venue quote needs.

Which view of trades answers the request: the caller's own, the workspace's,
a broker's umbrella, an LP's fills, or an LP's unsettled orders.

TradeRouteDisplay.description: The sold and bought sides of a trade for display read models.

dueAt.description: What it must settle by; absent unless `pending` or `overdue` with a known deadline.

settledAt.description: When it settled; absent unless `settled` and the time was recorded.

settledAtFill.description:
True when the trade settled at its fill (a prefunded venue balance, an on-chain fill),
so `settledAt` is the fill time; false otherwise. Absent when `withheld`.

TradeRowSettlementStatus.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

TradeSettlement.description: One trade's settlement as the taker: its lifecycle stages, transactions and LP response. The maker perspective is read by a signed-in member only.

TradeSettlementCarriedWindow.description:
The later window a delayed trade's amounts were carried into: its window obligations were
netted into that window's cumulative statement rather than paid. The trade settles there, by
`settlesBy` (the window's payment deadline, else its completion; absent while unconfirmed).

settlesBy.description: Payment deadline or completion time of the later window, or null if not confirmed.

windowId.description: Identifier of the later window into which the trade's obligations were netted.

TradeSettlementObligationList.description: The settlement obligations that reference one trade.

items.description: Settlement obligations for this trade on the current page.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

obligationId.description: Identifier of the obligation linked to this trade.

status.description: Current recorded status of the linked obligation.

venueAccountId.description: Identifier of the venue account the obligation settles.

windowId.description: Identifier of the settlement window for this trade link, or null when no window applies.

TradeSettlementState.description:
Where an executed trade's settlement stands: the same answer on the trade, its order and the
order's `order.updated` webhook. Absent before the trade fills (except `inTransit` and a
refunded on-chain trade's `failed`), and on a credit venue's trade recorded without
settlement terms. Clients must tolerate values added later.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

TradeSettlementStatement.description:
Whether the statement of the window a delayed trade settles in is out: `issued` once the
window's statement was produced, `failed` when producing it failed for good, else `pending`.
Absent on a trade that settles without a window. Clients must tolerate values added later.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

TradeVenueIdentity.description:
A trade's catalogue venue and execution method. Unknown historical membership is explicit;
it never acquires a venue or method from a stored display name.

executionMethod.description: Human execution-method label, or `Unknown method` when it cannot be resolved.

venueId.description:
Catalogue venue id: the one venue of a single-venue order or trade. An order executed at
several venues names each fill's venue on `fills[].venue`. Null when the recorded execution
type cannot be resolved.

venueName.description:
Catalogue product name of that one venue (per fill: `fills[].venue`), or `Unknown venue`
with the recorded id when unresolved.

TradingSource.description:
The exact source selected for a quote, retained through execution and recovery.

The wallet's financial-account id, or its own address on this network. A wallet named by
address is signed by the client, and need not be registered.

fillTx.description: Fill transaction reference on the destination network, or null when no fill hash is recorded.

The TetraFi-Version this webhook endpoint pinned when it was created; every body it receives is in that version.

available.description: The available balance read, as a decimal string in `units`.

observedAt.description: When the balance was read.

threshold.description: The rule's threshold, as a decimal string in `units`.

hash.description: Transaction hash recorded for this network.

amount.description: Unapplied portion of the movement, as a decimal string in `asset` units.

resource that could not be read (`wallets/<walletId>`). New sources may be added.

detail.description: One sentence naming the venue, what the order spends and where the rest stays.

rule.description:
The venue's rule that leaves the rest, in a few words for the card ("Binance trades USDC in
steps of 1"). Absent when the venue's step was not read; `detail` then says "fills whole lots".

effectiveFrom.description: When this scheduled change takes effect.

schedule.description: Complete fee schedule for the workspace once this change takes effect.

active.description: Whether to enable the subscription, omitted to keep its current setting.

omitted to keep its current pin. Deliveries enqueued after the change carry it.

How a token deployment represents its Asset: the Asset itself, or a 1:1
representation of it. A token with different economics is its own Asset, never a

VenueAccountCredit.description:
A venue account's credit: the same figures as the Treasury credit card. Each component is an
observation with its own time, or a named state (`notReported`, `notStarted`, `unavailable`
with its code); an unread figure is never zero.

commitments.description: TetraFi's own open credit commitments per currency.

facility.description: The agreed credit terms: the facility that stands without a provider-reported limit.

oneOf.description: Requested commitment consumers, or a named refusal; omitted without `include=consumers`.

included.x-undiscriminated-union-reason: Nullable value: JSON null has no properties and cannot carry a discriminator.

observation.description:
The provider's own credit line from the account's last recorded ledger observation:
limit, used, available and overrun (max(used - limit, 0)), in its currency.

positions.description: The account's signed positions per asset from the same ledger observation.

VenueTradeDispatch.description: The claimed venue submission and its recorded result. venueOrderId is the venue's native order identifier. Amounts are decimal currency units in the trade's debit and receipt assets; absent amounts are unknown, never zero. A sent order that filled nothing (outcomeCode confirmed_no_fill) says why in noFillReason, the venue's price then in noFill, whether placing again can work in retryable, and what to do next in remediation. Only the documented fields are part of the integrator contract; undocumented fields may be sent and must be ignored.

claimedAt.description: When the confirmed trade was claimed for dispatch.

confirmationKey.description: Idempotency key for the confirmation that claimed this trade.

confirmedQuoteId.description: Identifier of the quote accepted for this dispatch.

inputSpent.description: Amount actually spent as a decimal string in the debit asset's units, when recorded.

noFill.description:
The venue's price for the order's exact size after it filled nothing. Present only
beside `noFillReason`, when a price was read.

noFillReason.description:
Why a sent order filled nothing, when the venue's own answers say. Present only beside
`outcomeCode` `confirmed_no_fill`, and absent on a no-fill the venue gave no reason for.

outcomeCode.description: Stable sanitized classification, never an upstream response body.

outputReceived.description: Amount actually received as a decimal string in the receipt asset's units, when recorded.

quotedOutput.description:
The confirmed quote's output, beside `outputReceived`: a fill below it but
within the trade's minimum receipt is a normal fill (operator decision
2026-10-22), shown as "Received … (quoted …; within your minimum …)".

remediation.description:
What to do next. On a no-fill with `noFillReason`, `retry` with a fresh quote when the
order's own answer could get one, otherwise `requote`; absent when no reason was given.

retryable.description:
Whether placing again can work. On a no-fill: `true` when `noFillReason` names a reason
a new order can meet: a price kill (nothing was debited, and a fresh quote can fill) or
`transactionReverted` or `belowMinimumReceived` (nothing traded, only gas was spent; a new
quote prices the trade again), each with a `requote` or `retry` remedy; `false` when the venue gave no reason,
which includes a venue rejection that a retry would meet again. Absent on an outcome that
names no next step.

updatedAt.description: When the dispatch record was last updated.

venueOrderId.description: Order identifier assigned by the venue, when available.

A venue trade's execution status, in camelCase like the order `status` (`outcomeUnknown`).

treatment.description: How the fee was charged or reported for this fill.

fee.description: The venue's fee as recorded with the fill; absent before a fill.

legs.description:
Its payment legs (bank payout, pay-in, wallet payout), as the order page reads them:

quotedOutput.description: The confirmed quote's output, beside what was received.

How a venue-account Confirm is funded: the source the trader chose on Review.
Absent keeps the funding the venue and the firm ask's credit decision derive.

VenueTradeHistoryLeg.description: One leg of a venue trade in the trade history, named sell or buy as in POST /quotes. amount is the consented bound in exact decimal units of asset (on sell the most spent, on buy the least received); absent when not recorded, never zero.

amount.description:
The consented bound in exact decimal units of `asset`: on `sell` the most the trade may
spend, on `buy` the least it must receive. Absent when not recorded, never `0`.

asset.description: Asset sold or bought on this side of the trade.

VenueTradeNoFill.description: The venue's own price for the order's exact size, read after the order filled nothing.

currentPrice.description: The venue's price then, in the trade's market convention.

currentReceive.description: Exact decimal in the receipt asset: what the order's exact debit would receive at that price.

observedAt.description: When the venue stated that price.

slippageNeededBps.description:
The slippage from the quoted receive amount an order would have needed to fill at
that price, in basis points, rounded up. Absent when the quote's receive amount is
unknown; 0 when the price was at or above the quote.

VenueTradeNoFillReason.description:
Why a sent order filled nothing, when the venue's own answers say: `priceMoved` (the venue's price for the exact size moved outside the order's limit), `killedEveryAttempt` (every fill-or-kill order sent for the trade was killed), `priceUnreadable` (killed, and no fresh price could be read), `resendRefused` (killed, and the next send was refused before it left), `transactionReverted` (the trade's own on-chain transaction mined and reverted: nothing traded, only gas was spent), `belowMinimumReceived` (the trade's own swap mined and reverted because the pool would deliver less than its signed minimum, the price having moved past the swap's slippage tolerance: nothing traded, only gas was spent). Read with `noFill`. Treat an unknown value as a no-fill with no reason.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

VenueTradeNotSentReason.description:
Why a claimed trade was proven not sent. A cause TetraFi could not classify has its own value, never free text.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

VenueTradeOperation.description: A prepared or placed Basic venue trade. Track it by operationId and connectionId; executionStatus describes the trade and legsSettlementStatus where its legs' money movement stands; the trade's own settlement is the order's settlementStatus. steps lists each step the signing wallet was asked for, in order, with its status and transaction hash. initialReviewDisposition is the original planning verdict, not current approval. Only the documented fields are part of the integrator contract; undocumented fields may be sent and must be ignored.

order has no legs. Always present. The trade's own settlement is `settlementStatus`.

signing wallet and where it stands
(`pending`, `sent`, `mined`, `reverted`, `refused`, `lapsed`). Later typed signatures

The remedy for a venue trade that moved no money (`operation.dispatch.remediation`). A refusal
states only its kind, as the `details.remediation` token, with these operands beside it in `details`.

current price, in basis points, when known. Absent, never 0, when the price is at or above

VenueTradeRemediationKind.description:
What to do next: `retry` (place `quoteId`, a fresh quote for the same request and venue), `widenLimit` (place again with a minimum receive at least `requiredSlippageBps` below the quote), `requote` (ask the same venue for a new quote, then place that), `chooseAnotherLp` (this venue cannot take the trade now), `contactSupport` (something went wrong on TetraFi's side). their owner at the provider). Their page holds no factor of this wallet's
home, so it can't read its owners itself: their `confirm` asks TetraFi to
read them at the provider at that moment.

On the reader's own entry, when their slot names one of their wallets

stamps to approve as their member.

memberWalletOffers.description:
On the reader's own entry while they choose how they approve, and only when
the connection takes a wallet as a member on its key's curve: each of their
own wallets it would admit, with the exact bytes that wallet stamps. A pick
sends the wallet's id with one `memberWallet` proof over those bytes.

(`WALLET_MEMBER_WALLET_UNREADABLE`): a failed read, never "no wallets".

Set instead of `memberWallet` on the reader's own entry when their wallet's
approval bytes can't be given, naming why: the refusal its approval would
get (`WALLET_MEMBER_WALLET_INVALID`, `WALLET_MEMBER_FACTORS_BELOW_MINIMUM`,
`WALLET_MEMBER_CURVE_UNVERIFIED`, `WALLET_OWNERS_READ_PENDING`), or
`WALLET_MEMBER_WALLET_UNREADABLE` when it could not be read. A page shows
that reason, never an empty step.

its pick would be refused with (another provider, an unsupported network family, paused…).

when no name is recorded; absent only when their account records neither.
Never their user id.

needed.description: Number of factors this member must prove for their approval.

This person's factors as their own proofs proved them, in the form a page
matches against the owners of the provider. Empty for a person who has not
proven, and for every entry when the reader is not a person of the
creation; a factor no proof of this person proved is never listed.

Set instead of `ownerMatches` when this person's owners cannot be matched,
naming why: their stored proofs could not be read
(`WALLET_OWNER_MATCH_UNREADABLE`), or TetraFi keeps no proof of theirs
(`WALLET_OWNER_MATCH_NOT_KEPT`: they proved before what their proofs proved
was kept, or they left the wallet's owners, or it was retired). A page
refuses rather than treat them as none.

ownersConfirmedAt.description:
When this person's own signing page reported that its first-hand read of
the provider's owners found their own factors. Written only through their own
signing capability, never by anyone else (the creator included).

proven.description:
`true` once this person proved their factors on their signing page. The
provider holds nothing until the creator completes the creation.

yours.description:
`true` on the reader's own entry. A page that reads the owners first-hand
checks this person's factors itself and never accepts them from
`ownerMatches`; a page that shows TetraFi's readback names them as the
reader's own, as TetraFi reports them (a return visit holds no factor).

WalletCreationMemberWalletConsent.description:
The approval a person gives with one of their own wallets: the exact bytes
its root's factor stamps (a passkey, at the wallet's provider organisation),
sent back as a `memberWallet` proof. The bytes name this creation, signing
request, person and wallet, so the stamp approves nothing else.

address.description: Address of the member's approving wallet.

providerOrganizationId.description: The wallet's provider organisation, where its factor stamps.

walletId.description: Identifier of the member's existing wallet used for this approval.

WalletCreationMemberWalletRefusal.description:
One of a choosing person's own wallets that can't approve here, and why: the
code its pick is refused with, and the refusal's own words (one code covers
several causes: another provider, paused, owners unread).

WalletCreationOwnerMatch.description:
One factor of another person of a wallet being created, as that person's own
proof proved it, in the form a page matches against the provider's owners:
a passkey by its credential id, an external key by its curve and key, a login
(email, phone, Google account) by `matchToken`.

address.description: An external key's address, as picked.

credentialId.description: A passkey's credential id, as its attestation named it.

identity.description: The identity, masked as everywhere else (an external key's address in full).

kind.description: Type of proven owner factor to match against the provider's owner group.

matchToken.description:
A login's match token: the lowercase hex sha256 digest of the string's bytes
`tetrafi-owner-match:v1:{walletId}:{kind}:{identity}`, with `kind` the factor
kind's wire value (`emailCode`, `smsCode`, `google`) and the identity
normalized: an email trimmed and lowercased, a phone without whitespace or
`(`, `)`, `.`, `-`, a Google subject trimmed.

publicKey.description:
An external key's public key (hex, in its curve's compressed form where it has one), when
its proof recovered it.

WalletCreationPage.description: A page of the workspace's wallets being created, newest first.

included.description:
With `include=`: each listed wallet's connection (`connection`) and its capability
report (`capabilities`), keyed by `connectionId`, as their own reads answer this
caller, or `null` with that read's refusal. Absent otherwise.

items.description: Wallet creation records visible to the caller on this page.

nextCursor.description: Always present: the `cursor` for the next page, or null when there are no more pages.

WalletCreationReturn.description: Where an organisation wallet's approval page sends a person back, and who asked.

integratorName.description: Who asked for the wallet: the workspace's name when the wallet was asked for.

origin.description: Its origin (scheme, host and port), which the pages show.

url.description: The registered return URL the creation named.

WalletCreationScope.description:
Whose wallet is being created.

WalletCreationSigningRequest.description: The creation's signing request: its id, and the approval page each person of the wallet opens to set up their factors and approve.

approvalUrl.description:
The wallet's approval page in TetraFi (as on the wallet), to hand each
person of it.

id.description: Identifier of the caller's signing request for this wallet creation.

WalletCreationStatus.description:
The state of a wallet being created. Clients must read a value they do not know as not usable yet.

WalletCreationView.description: A wallet being created: what was asked for, who is still missing and where it stands.

address.description: The family address, once the provider created the wallet.

approvalUrl.description:
The wallet's approval page in TetraFi: each person of it (a personal
wallet's one owner too) opens this link, signs in, and proves or confirms
their own part on the signing page.

connectionId.description: Identifier of the wallet provider connection selected for creation.

countedPerMember.description: The people the creator confirmed count once per member they appear as.

createdAt.description: When the creation request was opened.

createdBy.description: The workspace user who started the creation.

creatorTradeGrant.description:
An organisation wallet's creator `trade` grant chosen with
`tradeFromThisWallet` (`notRequested` when it was not), read back from the
registered wallet's installed access policy; `pending` until the wallet is
registered and its creator acts on it in their own session. Absent for a
personal wallet.

displayName.description: Display name chosen for the wallet.

endedBy.description:
The id of the person who ended it before it was created: the creator who
cancelled it, or an invited owner who declined it. Absent otherwise.

expiresAt.description: When the pending creation expires if it is not completed.

failureCode.description: The named code of a failed or mismatched creation.

family.description: Network family of the wallet being created.

home.description:
Where the provider holds the wallet, once it created it (status `created`
or later): a pointer for reading its owners back, never proof of who owns it.

homeProvider.description: The provider that will hold the wallet's key and verify its owners.

id.description: The wallet id; it stays the wallet's id once created.

members.description: Owner group members and their progress through approval.

missing.description: The people who have not proven their factors yet.

networkNames.description:
The display name of each network in `networks`, keyed by its CAIP-2 id, as
the platform's network registry names it. A network the registry does not
name is absent here; it is never given a made-up label.

networks.description: CAIP-2 networks selected to be enabled when the wallet is created.

registeredAt.description:
When the active wallet was registered in the wallet directory, where it
is listed and used like any other wallet; absent until then.

registrationFailure.description:
Why the active wallet's last registration was refused (for example
`WALLET_REGISTRATION_AUTHORITY_LOST`); it is retried while absent from
the directory. Absent once registered.

returnTo.description: Where the approval page sends a person back, when the creation named a `returnUrl`.

scope.description: Whether the wallet being created is personal or belongs to the organisation.

signingRequestId.description:
The caller's own signing request, present only while the caller is a
person of this wallet who still has to act on it (the creator included,
until they complete it). Mint its capability with `POST
…/signing-requests/{signingRequestId}/capabilities`; a read never mints one.
Another person's request is never shown.

startedWithApiKey.description:
The API key its creator (`createdBy`) asked with; absent when they asked
in a signed-in session.

status.description: Current status of the wallet creation.

threshold.description: Number of owner approvals required under the group's counting rules.

workspaceId.description: Identifier of the workspace in which this creation was requested.

subject.description: Identifier of the Google account linked to this member's platform account.

The curve of a key. Clients must tolerate a value they do not know.

WalletLinkRecovery.description: Recovery for an explicitly chosen organisation wallet not linked to a Basic account.

defaultWallets.description:
Per CAIP-2 chain, the account's default wallets (target ids): a per-request switch the
caller sends as its pay-from preference, never a persistent preference write.

propertyNames.description:
A CAIP-2 chain id (`eip155:8453`, `solana:<genesis>`, `tron:shasta`), syntax-checked:
a namespace of 3 to 8 lowercase letters, digits or `-`, and a reference of 1 to 32
letters, digits, `-` or `_`. Compared exactly, as CAIP-2 references are case-sensitive.

linkHref.description: Relative link to the venue account's wallet linking controls.

wallet.description: Wallet that must be linked to the venue account before it can be used here.

The person who last switched it; absent when it was recorded from the wallet's creation or by
its provider.

enabled.description: Whether this network is enabled for the wallet.

network.description: The CAIP-2 network.

source.description: Who recorded the network.

WalletNetworkFacts.description:
A wallet's family and its networks, as a wallet read shows them.

`networksUnreadable` names why they could not be read
(`WALLET_NETWORKS_UNRECORDED`, `WALLET_FAMILY_UNREADABLE`,
`WALLET_NETWORKS_UNAVAILABLE`); then `family` is absent and `networks` is

family.description: The wallet's family: one key and one address on every network of it.

networks.description: Every network of the family recorded for the wallet, switched on or off.

networksUnreadable.description: Why the family and networks could not be read; absent when they were read.

WalletNetworkHoldings.description:
What TetraFi last observed held on a network. Switching a network off never moves or hides
funds: balances already there stay visible.

assets.description: The assets (symbols) last observed above zero on the network; empty unless `held`.

WalletNetworkHoldingsStatus.description:
What TetraFi last observed held on the network. Clients must read a value they do not know as not observed.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

WalletNetworkSource.description:
Who recorded the network. Clients must read a value they do not know as unknown.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

WalletStepAmount.description: An exact amount of one token, for display and for the backend re-check.

address.description:
The token's contract or mint address, in the network's own address format. The workspace's own step
record keeps its stored `token` key (`StoredWalletStepAmount`).

amount.description: Exact decimal in whole token units.

asset.description: The asset symbol the card shows (`USDC`).

WalletTransactionLanded.description:
Which retained transaction of a replaced send landed.

WebhookAutomationAmounts.description:
Present on a subscription to automation events: whether its deliveries
carry the definitions' amounts, and why not.

Whether automation event deliveries carry the definitions' amounts: `included`, `withheld` (the endpoint's principal may not see the amounts of at least one Automation, so those deliveries carry `amountVisibility` instead of amounts) or `unavailable` (access could not be read; deliveries withhold what cannot be decided). Clients must read a value they do not know as `withheld`.

active.description: Whether the subscription is enabled to receive deliveries.

Count of consecutive full-retry-schedule failures. Reset to 0 on any
successful delivery. Reaching 5 pauses the subscription.

createdAt.description: When the webhook endpoint was created.

events.description: Event types subscribed to by this endpoint.

id.description: Identifier of the configured webhook endpoint.

pausedAt.description:
Set when the subscription is auto-paused after persistent delivery
failure. Cleared when the subscription is reactivated.

updatedAt.description: When the webhook endpoint record was last updated.

url.description: URL to which webhook events are posted.

workspaceId.description: Identifier of the workspace that owns the webhook.

automationAmounts.description:
Present when the endpoint receives automation events: whether those
deliveries carry the definitions' amounts for its principal.

deliveryRetention.description:
How this endpoint's delivery history is kept: the retained receipts its `deliveries`
list can show, and whether they survive a server restart.

unreachable.description:
Present only on an update's answer whose delivery history could not be read after the
change was saved: one `lastDelivery` entry, and `lastDelivery` is then unknown, not

attempt.description: Number of attempts claimed so far for this delivery.

deliveredAt.description: Recorded time of the delivery result, whether or not the endpoint accepted it.

errorMessage.description: Diagnostic message for a failed or blocked attempt, when recorded.

The body as delivered, for a test delivery and for an event the log may show. Absent for
an event whose body is entitled by the subscription owner's read rights (order, settlement,
treasury and direct-user events): the log is readable with webhook management alone, so
read the resource the event names, or redeliver it to the endpoint.

redeliveryOf.description: Identifier of the delivery being resent, omitted for original deliveries.

test.description: Whether this is a test rather than an ordinary subscribed event delivery.

webhookId.description: Identifier of the configured endpoint for this delivery.

How an endpoint's delivery receipts are kept: `persistent_latest_receipts` survive a restart
(one latest receipt per delivery id), `process_memory` end with the server process; at most

scope.description: Whether delivery receipts persist across restarts or only live in process memory.

WebhookDeliverySummary.description: Summary of the newest retained delivery attempt.

at.description: When the most recent retained delivery attempt was recorded.

httpStatus.description: HTTP status returned by the endpoint, if it responded.

test.description: Whether the latest retained attempt was a test delivery.

info.description:
TetraFi is an API for institutional trading across on-chain and off-chain venues: discover assets, request quotes, place an order by quote id and read its status. API keys sign every request.

Asset-pair quotes: every tagged union is tagged by `kind`; only the outcome of `/prices` rows and `sources[]` entries is tagged by `status`.
info.title: TetraFi API

get.description: Lists the assets your workspace can trade, with their variants and networks. Call it first, and take the asset ids and networks for prices and quotes from it.

parameters.description: Assets per page, 1 to 200. May change between pages; omit it to keep the cursor's page size.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description:
The previous page's `nextCursor`. Valid while the workspace and ordered asset ids are
unchanged; otherwise answers 409 `CURSOR_STALE`. Asset metadata may change.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: `registry`: the registry snapshot the listing was built from, in `included.registry`.
parameters.name: include

parameters.description:
Only assets a venue offers this workspace, on-chain venues included: its venue id (`valr`,
every entry of it) or one venue entry (`valr-orderbook`, that entry only). With `venueCode`,
only the asset that venue's code is (`USC` at `b2c2` is USDC), and only when the instance the
code names, its variant included, is offered at that same venue or entry (`USDT0` is USDT
variant USDT0 at `valr-orderbook`, nothing at `valr-rfq`). Every filter narrows the listing;
an empty value answers 400 `ASSET_FILTER_BLANK` with `details.field` naming the filter.
parameters.name: venueId

parameters.description:
A venue's own code for an asset; needs `venueId` (otherwise 400 `ASSET_FILTER_INCOMPLETE`
with `details.field` `venueCode`).
parameters.name: venueCode

parameters.description:
Only assets with a deployment on this CAIP-2 network (`eip155:1`). With `address`, only the
asset deployed at that address there.
parameters.name: network

parameters.description:
A token address on `network`, in that chain's own form (EVM hex, Solana base58, Tron
base58check or hex; a form of another chain family matches nothing); needs `network` (otherwise 400 `ASSET_FILTER_INCOMPLETE` with `details.field`
`address`). A token the registry does not list matches nothing, whatever it
calls itself.
parameters.name: address

200.description: Workspace-eligible Assets with variants and CAIP-2 deployments. API keys require the prices_read scope.

RateLimit.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.1 structured dictionary, for example `limit=100, remaining=41, reset=19`. Remaining is the admitted decision's headroom; reset is whole seconds until quota next becomes available, not an epoch or a promise of a full burst refill. On a limiter's 429 remaining is 0 and reset equals Retry-After. Accepted key, route and per-address policies are compared by lowest remaining, then longest reset. A venue refusal without a known quota makes no rate-limit header claim.

RateLimit-Policy.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.5: quota and window in seconds, for example `100;w=60`. Sent on every status when a finite limiter counted the request. On a limiter's 429 this is exactly the policy that refused; if a venue discloses no quota, the headers are absent.

post.description: Order a quote you hold by its `id`, on its terms. Read it at its `statusUrl` until `terminal` is `true`. A refusal's `details.placementEffect` says whether an order may exist.

parameters.description: Makes a retry safe. Required for every caller, member session or API key (a missing key answers 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED). 1 to 255 bytes, unique per order you mean to place; a UUID is a good choice. A retry with the same key and the same body, from the same principal in the same workspace within 24 hours, returns the first answer and never places a second order. The same key with a different body answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; another principal's key answers 403 IDEMPOTENCY_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED. A retry that arrives while the first request is still running waits for it before any other check (an expired quote or price included), answers what the first request answered, and answers 409 ORDER_IN_PROGRESS (with Retry-After) if it is still running after 30 seconds. A retry after a first request that may have placed an order (it stopped without an answer, or was refused with `details.placementEffect` `uncertain`) answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN before any other check, with no Retry-After: retrying that key can never settle it, so read the orders back (GET /api/v1/orders, details.readTarget) and use a new key only once the order is not there. One `uncertain` refusal releases its key: a source transaction's registration refused while its receipt is pending or unreadable; send the same request again once the transaction is readable (the quote still places at most one order). A refusal marked `noOrder` is not stored: fix the request and send it again with the same key or a new one.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: Signed-in sessions whose member turned on the check for orders: a step-up proof for purpose `order_placement` bound to this quote. Ignored for API keys.
parameters.name: X-Step-Up-Proof

requestBody.description: The required `kind` selects the order. `quote`: order a quote you hold by its `quoteId`, on its terms. `stream`: order a tradable Live prices row by its `priceId` (a row size's id from GET /prices, ordered before its `validFor` lapses) with exactly one limit, `minReceive` or `slippageBps` (0 to 9999, measured from the receive amount that price states and rounded up to the receive Asset's precision). A missing or unknown `kind` answers 400 INVALID_REQUEST with `details.field` `kind`. Treat the set of kinds as open.

200.description: Order created: a `basicTrade` (or `advancedTrade`) order. An on-chain Basic trade answers `working` before its wallet signs; read the order for its outcome.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when this answer was released from the stored receipt of an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key and body, rather than produced now. Absent on a first answer.

409.description: PRICE_EXPIRED: a stream order's priceId lapsed (its validFor passed); read Live prices again, nothing was sent. PRICE_ACCOUNT_NOT_PRICED: the venue account a stream order's priceId was read on has no orderable price now (details.cause `connectionNotFound` or `otherAccountPriced`); it is never ordered on another account, and nothing was sent. QUOTE_ALREADY_ORDERED: this quote already placed an order (details.orderId names it when known), or the CEX route cannot be ordered as signed; LEGACY_CEX_LANE_RETIRED. QUOTE_NOT_EXECUTABLE (`next: requote`), QUOTE_ALREADY_ORDERED, QUOTE_NOT_HELD (`next: requote`), FUNDING_SHORTFALL (`next: fund`), VENUE_QUOTE_OUTSIDE_BOUNDS, VENUE_QUOTE_NOT_PRICED; a bank card: FIAT_CARD_NOT_A_BANK_CARD, FIAT_CARD_ACCOUNT_UNREADABLE, FIAT_BANK_ACCOUNT_UNBOUND (choose the bank account to be paid on the quote card, then requote), FIAT_PAYOUT_FEE_UNVERIFIED, FIAT_FUNDING_MISMATCH, and the hosted Confirm's named conflicts (VENUE_TRADE_RECONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, VENUE_TRADE_PAYOUT_DESTINATION_CHANGED); a Treasury review that can no longer approve the trade, nothing sent: VENUE_TRADE_REVIEW_REJECTED (rejected or cancelled), VENUE_TRADE_REVIEW_EXPIRED (expired, or reapproval required); VENUE_OPERATION_MISMATCH (the named `operationId` does not cover the quote); a protocol quote: PAY_WALLET_UNAVAILABLE (the held binding's pay wallet is no longer available to the caller)

get.description: Lists the directed asset pairs your workspace can trade now, each with the routes (venue and where it executes) that serve it, one page at a time. `availability=connectable` lists instead the pairs only a venue you have not connected, not finished setting up or paused would serve.

parameters.description: Only pairs selling this asset id (`USDC`).
parameters.name: sellAsset

parameters.description: Only pairs buying this asset id.
parameters.name: buyAsset

parameters.description: Only pairs with this asset id on either side.
parameters.name: asset

parameters.description:
Only routes of this venue entry (`binance-orderbook`); a pair with none left is not listed.
A route of several legs is venue `composite` (`venueId=composite` lists those).
parameters.name: venueId

parameters.description: Only routes with either leg on this CAIP-2 network (`eip155:1`); off-chain routes are left out.
parameters.name: network

parameters.description: `enabled` (default) or `connectable`.
parameters.name: availability

parameters.description:
Pairs per page: 100 when omitted, at most 1000 (a larger value is served as 1000). A page
may hold fewer; only a null `nextCursor` ends the listing. May change between pages.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description:
The previous page's `nextCursor`, sent with the same filters (otherwise 400
`CURSOR_INVALID`). Opaque: never build or edit one.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Comma-separated top-level fields of each pair to return (`fields=id` lists pair ids only); id, sell and buy are always kept. JSON only
parameters.name: fields

200.description: One page of the workspace's pairs. API keys require the prices_read scope.

post.description: One request covers every venue your workspace can use, and filters narrow it. You get `quotes`, best first, and each venue's outcome in `sources`; `answeredFrom` says where the answer came from: `venues` when any venue was contacted, `cache` otherwise. Order a quote by its `id`.

parameters.description: Makes a retry safe; optional. 1 to 255 bytes; a UUID is a good choice. A retry with the same key and the same body, from the same credential's owner in the same workspace within 24 hours, returns the first answer (header Idempotent-Replayed: true; its quotes may have expired since) and asks no venue again. The same key with a different body answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; a retry while the first is still running waits for its answer. Refusals are not stored. Not accepted with Accept: text/event-stream (400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID): a streamed answer cannot be replayed.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

sources.detail: This account is still being set up. Finish its activation in Venues before requesting prices.

200.description: A PairQuoteSet: quotes, best first, and every venue's outcome in sources. Accept: text/event-stream streams it as quote, source, complete and error events.

On a limiter's 429 remaining is 0 and reset equals Retry-After. Accepted key, route and per-address policies are compared by lowest remaining, then longest reset. A venue refusal without a known quota makes no rate-limit header claim.

RateLimit-Policy.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.5: quota and window in seconds, for example `100;w=60`. Sent on every status when a finite limiter counted the request. The applicable policy closest to exhaustion is reported (section 3.2): lowest remaining, then longest reset. On a limiter's 429 this is exactly the policy that refused; if a venue discloses no quota, the headers are absent.

get.description: Lists your workspace's trades, newest first: orders placed through TetraFi and trades on your venue accounts. Filter by kind, order status, settlement status and time, and page with the cursor.

parameters.description: Workspace ID
parameters.name: workspaceId

parameters.description:
mine, workspace or umbrella. Default: workspace. umbrella needs a broker
workspace and permission to view its clients' compliance records; mine needs a
member session.
parameters.name: scope

parameters.description:
taker (default, in every workspace) or maker. maker needs an LP workspace and
permission to view settlements.
parameters.name: perspective

parameters.description:
all, order or venueTrade. Default: all for taker and umbrella; for maker the
fills default (on-chain orders); umbrella has orders only.
parameters.name: kind

parameters.description:
The trade's order status, matched against a row's `status` (`PublicOrderStatus`, the value
its order read answers). Taker projections (mine, workspace) only; a venue trade has none,
so `kind=all` leaves venue trades out by name.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description:
Recorded settlement, matched against a row's `settlementStatus`. Taker: pending, settled,
failed, refunded or unknown (none recorded); maker: the fill's settlement; umbrella: the
record's settlementStatus.
parameters.name: settlementStatus

parameters.description:
Counterparty: the LP's catalogue venue id, the row's `lpVenueId` (taker; a venue
trade matches its execution type's venue) or an LP workspace UUID (orders only), the client workspace (umbrella) or the
taker (maker).
parameters.name: counterpartyId

parameters.description: LP workspace id, across every product and execution method of that LP.
parameters.name: lpId

parameters.description: Execution outcome, independently of settlement: filled, notFilled or pending.
parameters.name: fillOutcome

parameters.description: Exact execution-type identity: the maker of an order (taker), or one of the LP's own venues (maker).
parameters.name: venueId

parameters.description:
The member or client who placed the order: member (taker), user id (umbrella),
entity (maker).
parameters.name: client

parameters.description: Settlement stage of an unsettled order (maker only).
parameters.name: settlementStage

parameters.description: Only orders at least this many seconds old (maker only, with settlementStage).
parameters.name: minAgeSeconds

parameters.description: Placed at or after this RFC 3339 instant.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Placed at or before this RFC 3339 instant (umbrella: a UTC midnight).
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Page size; the projection's own bounds apply (default 25).
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The nextCursor of the previous page.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: json (default) or csv. csv returns the projection's export of the same filters.
parameters.name: format

parameters.description: Taker: comma-separated lifecycle buckets (inProgress, completed, failed, refunded, unknown). Maker: the fills lifecycle filter
parameters.name: lifecycle

parameters.description: Taker: taker, support, counterparty or none
parameters.name: nextActor

parameters.description: Taker: a registry asset id (`USDC`) either side resolves to; an unlisted id is 400
parameters.name: asset

parameters.description: Corridor (source-dest)
parameters.name: corridor

parameters.description: Taker: linked wallet id
parameters.name: walletId

parameters.description: Taker: wallet address (custody vault or linked wallet)
parameters.name: address

parameters.description: The row's routingPath type: direct or via_broker
parameters.name: routingPath

parameters.description: Lowest USD value (`valueUsd`), a decimal string; a trade with no recorded USD value is not listed
parameters.name: valueUsdMin

parameters.description: Highest USD value (`valueUsd`), a decimal string; a trade with no recorded USD value is not listed
parameters.name: valueUsdMax

parameters.description: field (ascending) or -field (descending). Every projection: createdAt. Taker: valueUsd, settlementStatus, corridor, counterparty, member (workspace scope), orderId, settlementSpeedSeconds. Umbrella: valueUsd. Maker: settlementStatus, orderId. A cursor pages only the order it was returned for
parameters.name: sort

parameters.description: Comma-separated top-level fields of each row to return; tradeId, kind, projection, id and status are always kept. JSON only
parameters.name: fields

parameters.description: Related objects to expand into `included`, comma-separated: `settlement`, each listed trade's settlement by `tradeId`, as `GET …/trades/{tradeId}/settlement` answers this caller in the row's perspective, or null with that read's refusal. Unknown relation 400 `INCLUDE_UNKNOWN`, malformed or repeated 400 `INCLUDE_INVALID`; not on a signed API-key request or with format=csv
parameters.name: include

parameters.description: Taker: only orders whose nextAction is present
parameters.name: actionRequired

200.description: One page of trades; with format=csv, the projection's CSV of the same filters

Remaining is the admitted decision's headroom; reset is whole seconds until quota next becomes available, not an epoch or a promise of a full burst refill. On a limiter's 429 remaining is 0 and reset equals Retry-After. Accepted key, route and per-address policies are compared by lowest remaining, then longest reset. A venue refusal without a known quota makes no rate-limit header claim.

RateLimit-Policy.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.5: quota and window in seconds, for example `100;w=60`. Sent on every status when a finite limiter counted the request. The applicable policy closest to exhaustion is reported (section 3.2): lowest remaining, then longest reset. On a limiter's 429 this is exactly the policy that refused; if a venue discloses no quota, the headers are absent.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always sent on 429; sent on 503 when the wait is known. `details.retryAfter` carries the same wait as an ISO 8601 duration.

get.description: Read the deposits a venue credited to the account over up to 30 days, for every asset and network asked for in one read (comma lists; omit them for all). Items arrive oldest first; a pair that could not be read is named in `unreachable`, never shown as empty.

parameters.description: Current company or broker workspace
parameters.name: workspaceId

parameters.description:
Assets the credits moved, comma-separated (any of). Omit for every asset the venue offers
for deposit on the account's site.
parameters.name: asset

parameters.description:
CAIP-2 networks the credits moved on, comma-separated (any of). Omit for every network. An
asset the venue declares no network for is read by asset only, whatever this asks.
parameters.name: network

parameters.description:
Window start, RFC 3339: 1 to 30 whole days before now (default 7 days back); the window
ends now. On later pages the cursor's frozen window applies; omit `from` then.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description:
Credits per page across every pair, 1 to 200. Omit for all credits; a cursor retains its
page size.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The previous page's nextCursor. Ask with the same `asset` and `network`.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description:
`observation` (each pair's observation in `included.observation[<pair>]`) and/or
`connection` (the connection in `included.connection[venueAccountId]`), comma-separated.
parameters.name: include

200.description: A provider without qualified deposit history: no credits, and the history named unreachable

get.summary: Read the venue account's deposit history

get.description: Read where to deposit into a venue account: an address for an asset and network, or bank details for a fiat asset sent without a network.

parameters.description: Current company or broker workspace
parameters.name: workspaceId

parameters.description:
The asset to deposit. With `network`, a digital asset whose deposit address is read;
alone, an ISO 4217 fiat asset (`USD`) whose bank-deposit instructions are read.
parameters.name: asset

parameters.description: The CAIP-2 network to deposit a digital `asset` on.
parameters.name: network

parameters.description: The dedicated fiat venue's linked bank id for the sending bank. Required with a fiat asset for a dedicated fiat venue and refused for other venues.
parameters.name: providerBankId

parameters.description:
One of the venue account's open pay-in legs (a summary pay-in window's `legId`):
the read selects that leg's asset and, for a dedicated fiat venue, the paying
bank its deposit declaration recorded. Only on the venue-account read, and never
with `asset`, `network` or `providerBankId`.
parameters.name: payInLegId

bankDeposit.reason: The deposit reference was read from the bound venue account. The venue does not publish its receiving bank details over its API: its own app shows them next to this reference. No deposit has been confirmed.

expectedArrival.source: VALR S20 https://support.valr.com/hc/en-us/articles/360028737292 "How long does it take for my Rand (ZAR) deposit to reflect in my VALR account?" (updated 2026-10-12T13:34:54Z, retrieved 2026-10-15)

capabilities.reason: Independent account evidence is not implemented for this provider.

example.reason: The deposit reference was read from the bound venue account. The venue does not publish its receiving bank details over its API: its own app shows them next to this reference. No deposit has been confirmed.

200.description: Deposit instructions for the venue account.

On a limiter's 429 remaining is 0 and reset equals Retry-After. Accepted key, route and per-address policies are compared by lowest remaining, then longest reset. A venue refusal without a known quota makes no rate-limit header claim.

RateLimit-Policy.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.5: quota and window in seconds, for example `100;w=60`. Sent on every status when a finite limiter counted the request. The applicable policy closest to exhaustion is reported (section 3.2): lowest remaining, then longest reset. On a limiter's 429 this is exactly the policy that refused; if a venue discloses no quota, the headers are absent.

get.description: Lists the wallets being created on your workspace's wallet connections, newest first, each with its status and the people who have not approved yet. Use it to find the creations waiting for you.

parameters.description: Workspace ID
parameters.name: workspaceId

parameters.description: Comma-separated statuses (`pending`, `creating`, `uncertain`, `created`, `active`, `readbackMismatch`, `failed`, `expired`).
parameters.name: status

parameters.description:
`me`: only the wallets with your own signing request open (factors to prove
while pending, or the created wallet's owners to confirm), at any status.
parameters.name: assignee

parameters.description: Related objects to expand into `included`, comma-separated, each keyed by the wallets' `connectionId`. `connection`: the wallet's connection exactly as `GET …/wallet-providers/setup-connections` lists it to this caller, or null with that list's refusal (403 without View wallets, 403 `JWT_REQUIRED` for an API key) or 404 `WALLET_CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND` for a connection the workspace no longer has. `capabilities`: its capability report exactly as `GET …/wallet-providers/connections/{connectionId}/capabilities` answers this caller, or null with that read's refusal. Unknown relation 400 `INCLUDE_UNKNOWN`, malformed or repeated 400 `INCLUDE_INVALID`; not on a signed API-key request.
parameters.name: include

RateLimit.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.1 structured dictionary, for example `limit=100, remaining=41, reset=19`. Remaining is the admitted decision's headroom; reset is whole seconds until quota next becomes available, not an epoch or a promise of a full burst refill. On a limiter's 429 remaining is 0 and reset equals Retry-After. Accepted key, route and per-address policies are compared by lowest remaining, then longest reset. A venue refusal without a known quota makes no rate-limit header claim.

RateLimit-Policy.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.5: quota and window in seconds, for example `100;w=60`. Sent on every status when a finite limiter counted the request. The applicable policy closest to exhaustion is reported (section 3.2): lowest remaining, then longest reset. On a limiter's 429 this is exactly the policy that refused; if a venue discloses no quota, the headers are absent.
